text: Marshall von Hindenburg has yielded to persuasion to stand for the Presidency.

label: text
text: [Yesterday's cables stated that in spite of the German Nationals' desperate efforts, Marshal Von Hindenburg had declined to accept nomination for the Presidency. He declared that he did not intend at this age to enter politics from which he had all his life held aloof. It was understood that, Hindenburg's refusal was influenced by the absence of support from the German People's Party. Herr Stresemann, the Foreign Minister, who is one of the leaders, pointed out the disastrous impression, such a candidacy would make in Europe. Later the Nationals despatched Admiral von Tirpitz to Hanover to try to induce Hindenburg to change his mind,

text:
The Commonwealth Government has accepted the proposals of the Government of New South Wales for the construction of a floating Dock at Walsh Island.
The Dock is to have a displacement of 13,000 tons and is to take two years to build.
The Commonwealth Government will contribute £12,000 towards the cost.

label: text
text: The dock will be used for commercial purposes, but in time of war or any other emergency the Commonwealth Government will take control.

text: O'Slo, April 8.—The City of Oslo has contracted a loan of eight million dollars with the New York bankers, Kuhd and Loeb. The period is thirty years and interest 6 per cent.—Router.

label: text
text: In the House of Commons at question time, Mr. J. C. Davison, Parliamentary and Financial Secretary to the Admiralty, said the Government would gladly cooperate with the other principal Powers in any further restriction of naval armaments.

label: text
text: They had already drawn much attention to the subject but the publication of a reasoned statement of British naval needs as a basis for the limitation of naval armaments; as suggested by the questioner, would not conclude to this end, nor would it be of public interest.

label: text
text: Sir Henry Page-Croft (Conservative) declared that Britain had decreased her naval armaments to far larger extent than any other naval Power in the world.

label: text
text: Sir J. Nail (Conservative) asked for an assurance that in any further conference British naval power would not be reduced disproportionately to that of other Powers.

label: text
text: Mr. Davison said the question was hypothetical.

label: text
text: The Secretary for Foreign Affairs, Mr. Austen Chamberlain, replied that representations had been and were being made both to Peking and Mukden to secure the return of the section.

label: text
text: Asked whether he did not think the time had arrived to consult the other Powers interested with a view to taking definite steps to get a settled position in China, Mr. Chamberlain said he had been in communication with the other Powers concerned and if he saw an opportunity of advantageously taking any steps he would do so.

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, replying to a question suggesting that representations should be made to China to speed up the trial or to procure the release of the Russian railway officials Ostroumoff and Gandatti who are imprisoned at Harbin, Mr. Austen Chamberlain said that he was seeking the report on the case before deciding whether action was possible or desirable.

text: Before the Committee of Industry and Trade witnesses on behalf of the Federation of Master Cotton Spinners' Associations referred to competition by Japan in India and the East generally and from local productions.

label: text
text: They expressed the opinion that the present “difficulty of the absence of bulk trade was due mainly to the high price of the raw material and the impoverishment of the main consuming countries.

label: text
text: They considered that commercial supremacy in cotton goods could not be seriously challenged with reduced taxation and longer working hours.

label: text
text: A witness on behalf of the Manchester Cotton Association suggested as regards raw cotton that certain Empire cottons should be made, tenderable against Liverpool futures. A contract would thus receive proper status and expedite their development to that extent.
